851d333c28: Main grooveMain RhythmDecides the music's main style. Drums and bass carry the whole song's groove.

9c2b5c6683: Lead melodyLeadThe piece's main role: the voice, or a solo instrument.
88c64c48b6: FillsFill InConnect sections and fill gaps. Unlike the secondary groove, fills don't repeat on a regular pattern.

08c5dbeed2: BuildThe rule of four, and open, build, turn, close
ec9e6df491: Lay out section lengths in multiples of four
1075768dc9: Every section is at least two bars (eight beats), usually four or eight bars. Listeners' ears are used to counting in fours, so when sections fall on multiples of four, the changes feel most natural.
1f58e71c14: When practising arranging: open (intro) two bars, build (theme) four bars, turn (chorus) four bars, close (outro) two bars. Once you're fluent, expand it to 4-8-8-4.
60b6502201: BuildHow vocals and arrangement relate
109734596b: An arrangement's first job: let the voice come through clearly
ed62f5dd0c: When the voice is singing, other instruments step back; when it takes a breath, a fill steps in.
499b7b1023: Don't cram too many instruments into the middle range where the voice sits. The verse piano is often placed lower or higher than the voice.
077413d838: The arrangement follows the lead singer's key. If the key changes, every instrument has to be rearranged.
cc87d02aa1: A good vocal decides eighty per cent of a song. However lavish the arrangement, if it covers the lyrics, listeners lose the story.
